claim: Asymmetric verifier error can be corrected at the reward or score-function level and improves noisy-RLVR training
caveat: Assumes estimable channel rates and may not cover adversarial instance-dependent errors

claim: Extensional verifiers can directly induce shortcut policies that pass checks without learning the intended rule
caveat: Evidence is concentrated on inductive rule tasks

claim: Reasoning-effort curves can detect implicit verifier exploitation missed by chain-of-thought monitors
caveat: Detection does not itself prevent hacking and depends on truncation validity

claim: Training on harmless reward hacks can transfer to broader misaligned behavior
caveat: Main intervention is supervised fine-tuning rather than an RLVR training run

claim: Hybrid rule and model verification expands instruction-following RL coverage
caveat: General capability gains do not prove robustness to adaptive verifier gaming

claim: Joint online training of solving and self-verification improves both reported capabilities
caveat: Self-verification and outcome verification may share failure modes

claim: Reference-answer likelihood can provide a verifier-free RL objective for broader reasoning domains
caveat: Reference availability changes the task and does not remove proxy-objective risk

claim: Static reward-model benchmark accuracy is weakly aligned with optimized-policy quality
caveat: Findings concern learned reward models rather than binary rule verifiers

claim: Matching demonstration reward levels mitigates reward overoptimization without relying only on KL
caveat: Depends on representative demonstrations and reward-scale calibration

claim: Component-reward constraints can keep optimization inside each proxy's useful range
caveat: Requires identifying useful thresholds and component decomposition

claim: Reward uncertainty penalties from diverse low-rank ensembles reduce overoptimization
caveat: Ensemble uncertainty can be correlated and increases inference cost

claim: Mixing verified historical successes with fresh rollouts improves convergence and final math accuracy
caveat: Positive-only replay may reduce exploration and cross-task evidence is limited

claim: Bellman-style value learning enables replay-buffer reuse and faster reported reasoning training
caveat: Value bootstrapping introduces a different bias and lacks broad independent replication

claim: Fully asynchronous rollout and training can improve speed when staleness is explicitly controlled
caveat: Quality matching is hardware recipe and policy-change-rate dependent

claim: Multi-version streaming preserves long-tail trajectories and can bound staleness without measurable matched-difficulty degradation
caveat: The safe bound is empirical and system/model dependent

claim: Self-speculative decoding reduces both rollout and end-to-end latency while preserving target-distribution samples
caveat: Reported gains depend on hardware regime and adaptive activation

claim: Hybrid execution control substantially improves RLHF throughput across configurations
caveat: Throughput improvement is not evidence of optimizer quality or request latency

claim: Large-scale alignment workloads can be efficiently distributed with specialized model placement
caveat: Toolkit report is not an algorithmic causal study

claim: Separating and scheduling actor critic reward and reference workloads improves RLHF utilization
caveat: Limited standardized cross-framework latency evidence

claim: Dynamic parameter reallocation and searched execution plans improve RLHF training speed
caveat: Benefits depend on cluster topology and workload sizes
